text: The development of chemical processes is closely linked to human demands for material transformation. From ancient activities such as brewing and pottery making, to modern processes like ammonia synthesis and petrochemical production, and to contemporary fields like polymer materials and fine chemicals, the core objective has always been to achieve the transformation from laboratory chemical reactions to large-scale industrial production through optimizing process routes, equipment design, and operating conditions. Association with "Chemical Engineering": Chemical processes focus more on "processes and products" (such as ammonia synthesis process, pharmaceutical process), while chemical engineering focuses more on "common technologies and equipment" (such as heat transfer, mass transfer, reaction engineering). The two complement each other and jointly constitute the core of the chemical discipline.Core characteristics: Based on chemical principles, combined with knowledge from engineering, materials science, economics, etc., it solves industrialization problems such as "how to produce, how much to produce, how to reduce costs, and how to reduce pollution".
